Now I can see the vulnerable code clearly. At line 7981:
```c
if(ndpi_str->cfg.tcp_fingerprint_raw_enabled)
    flow->tcp.fingerprint_raw = ndpi_strdup(options_fp);
```

When `options_len == 0`, the `options_fp` buffer is never written to (the `else` branch with the options loop is skipped). So `options_fp` contains uninitialized stack data, and `ndpi_strdup(options_fp)` calls `strlen()` on it.

Also, when `tcp_fingerprint_format == NDPI_MUONFP_TCP_FINGERPRINT`, the `options_fp` is never written to even when `options_len > 0`, because the code only writes to `options_fp` in the `NDPI_NATIVE_TCP_FINGERPRINT` case.

My PoC sets `tcp_fingerprint_raw=1` and sends a TCP SYN packet with no options (options_len == 0). This should trigger the vulnerability.
